questions.q: Why is common sense unreliable when making predictions?
a: It ignores the cognitive biases that shape decisions
It relies on far too much data
It changes with every generation
It only applies to small groups
questions.why: Lesson 1 says biases make common sense unstable.

questions.q: What explains Austria's high organ donor rate?
a: Donation is the default and people must opt out
Austrians are naturally more generous
Doctors ask every citizen in person
The law requires everyone to donate
questions.why: Lesson 1 contrasts opt-out defaults with Germany's opt-in system.

questions.q: What does Zara's measure and react approach avoid?
a: Predicting demand in advance
Listening to customers
Testing small samples of new items
Following emerging fashion trends
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Zara reacts to what shoppers already wear.

questions.q: What is local knowledge, as the summary uses the term?
a: Insight from people closest to the work
Data purchased from Google or Facebook
Advice from outside consultants
National sales statistics
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to ask the people who already do the work.

questions.q: What does Watts mean by uncommon sense?
a: Decisions grounded in the scientific method
Instincts sharpened by years of experience
The consensus of a large group
Rules handed down by experts
questions.why: Lesson 3 says uncommon sense tests hypotheses with data.
